intro.title: Build token revocation list in Redis
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a token revocation list using Redis to manage and invalidate access tokens in a Node.js application. You will learn how to store and check revoked tokens in Redis, a fast in-memory data store, to enhance security by preventing the use of compromised tokens. The core programming concept involves using Redis commands like SET and GET to handle key-value pairs for token management. You'll implement functions to add tokens to the revocation list and verify if a token is revoked, applying basic JavaScript and asynchronous operations. By the end, you'll have a functional revocation system that integrates with Node.js to secure your applications.
intro.usecase: Token revocation lists are essential security features in production authentication systems. When users log out or administrators need to terminate compromised sessions, services like banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and enterprise admin panels use Redis-based revocation to immediately invalidate JWT tokens. This prevents unauthorized access to sensitive user data, transaction histories, or admin controls even if tokens haven't technically expired. Developers implement this pattern to meet security compliance requirements while maintaining fast session management across distributed applications.
